Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) is one of the largest universities in Germany. Thanks to its location in the Rhine-Main science region, the university can unfold to its full potential and showcase its innovative power and dynamism. Its status as a comprehensive university allows for multidisciplinary learning and teaching and has great potential for internationally renowned, interdisciplinary research. Almost all of its institutes are located on a single campus close to the Mainz city center - creating a lively academic culture for researchers, teaching staff, and students from every continent.Academic staff member (Postdoc): Plant RNA BiologyThe Wachter group investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants (https://mps-imp.biologie.uni-mainz.de/). Our recent work has identified novel components of the plant splicing-regulatory code, including structured mRNA elements (e.g., https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.71060 ) and position-dependent functions of pyrimidine motifs (https://doi.org/10.1111/tpj.16739). By combining these functional studies with global profiling approaches, we are building a framework to understand and engineer alternative splicing in the context of plant development and stress responses.As a member of our international research team, you will examine the regulation and functional impact of splicing decisions controlled by polypyrimidine tract-binding proteins (PTBs), a family of key splicing regulators in plants and animals. Your work will build on our previous findings on PTB functions in alternative splicing and on recent results from ongoing transcriptome-wide approaches, including splicing pattern profiling, iCLIP, and TRIBE. You will further develop these analysis pipelines and integrate the resulting datasets to define the role of this central component of splicing control in the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana. The new insights from these mechanistic studies will be linked to physiological PTB functions we previously observed, including ABA-dependent seed germination and drought tolerance. The overarching goal of this project is to establish the molecular connections between PTB functions and key traits of stress physiology, thereby laying the groundwork for novel strategies to enhance plant resilience. This work is supported by extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure.Tackling critical questions on PTB functions in A. thaliana using a multidisciplinary approach, which integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, and plant stress physiologyApplying state-of-the-art techniques for gene-specific and genome-wide analyses of RNA biologyDeveloping an integrated framework to decipher PTB’s role in splicing and its downstream physiological outcomes, with a particular focus on drought stressAssisting with lab organisation and other general tasksContributing to teaching activities for Bachelor's and Master's students within our groupSupervising PhD students and other group membersPresenting your research findings in oral and written form, including conference contributions, reports, and manuscriptsA successfully completed scientific university degree in Biology or in a related fieldA successfully completed doctorate (PhD) in molecular plant biology or RNA biologyExperience with a spectrum of molecular methodsExperience in plant (stress) physiology is a plus, but not mandatoryTeaching experience is a plus, but not mandatoryVery good English language skills (at least level B2); German language skills are a plus, but not mandatoryA successful academic track record documented by publications, conference contributions, etc.A fascination for science, very good communication and teamwork skillsIn addition to the general requirements according to public services law, applicants must meet the recruitment requirements stipulated in § 57 of the Hochschulgesetz of ...

jobs.description: General informationThe new Chair of Behavioral Accounting ( Prof. Dr. Victor van Pel t) at WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management in Vallendar is dedicated to the empirical and experimental analysis of decision-making behavior in accounting settings. The focus is on behavioral accounting, controlled, online, and field experiments, and contemporary trends like the use of artificial intelligence. Our research examines how controls, performance feedback, and reporting choices shape the judgments and decisions of managers, employees, investors, and other firm stakeholders. WHU has an international orientation, offers an excellent research environment, and has a vibrant doctoral programme. Moreover, our chair is part of the Finance and Accounting Group, which organizes frequent reading groups and research seminars that further strengthen your doctoral training. This position is particularly suited for people (f/m/d) interested in behavioral research, with a focus on accounting questions, and a career in academia.Your mission Research• Conducting independent research in the field of behavioral accounting, in particular on experimental issues in reporting, controls, performance feedback, and the use of artificial intelligence in accounting.• The aim is to present research results at international conferences and publish them in leading journals.Teaching• Collaboration in the implementation and further development of courses in the field of financial and management accounting (e.g. preparation of materials, supervision of students, data analysis or support with experiments).• Opportunity to gradually take on your own teaching responsibilities and further develop your teaching skills as part of your doctoral programme.Doctoral programme• Active participation in WHU’s structured doctoral programme, which includes methodological and theoretical courses, research seminars, and presentations in the doctoral colloquium.• Use of the international research environment for professional and personal development, including access to laboratory and online recruitment resources and support for conference travel.Your profileAcademic background• Above-average master’s degree in accounting, economics, finance or a related area.• Ideally, your master’s thesis was written in a subject area related to behavioral or experimental research.• We particularly value if you’ve finished a preparation track, like a research master or another specialized graduate research program.Technical and methodological skills• Strong mathematical programming, analytical, and critical thinking skills.• Experience with experimental design, statistical inference, and academic research and writing practices.• Proficiency in at least one of the following statistical programming languages: R, Stata, or Python.• Experience with oTree for conducting experiments is a big plus.Research interests• Strong interest in experimental behavioral research, particularly in the areas of accounting.• Interest in topics such as misreporting, performance measurement and feedback, controls, incentives, and contemporary issues like sustainability and the use of AI is particularly welcome.Personal requirements• A passion for learning and scientific research in an international environment.• Excellent written and spoken English proficiency (German proficiency is not required).What we offer Academic EnvironmentWHU has more than 60 faculty members in the fields of management, finance and accounting, economics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing and sales, and supply chain management. Research at WHU aims to adhere to three principles: quality, internationality, and practical relevance.WHU is an equal opportunity employer and thus welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds. We believe in the benefits of diversity and therefore foster an international, inclusive, and inspiring working environment.ContactFor questions please contact:Professor Victor van Peltemail: Victor.vanPelt@whu.eduAbout usAs one of Germany’s top private business schools, WHU is consistently ranked among Europe’s finest. At both the Vallendar and Düsseldorf campuses, we empower leaders to become responsible changemakers, guided by integrity, diversity, and strengthened by a deep sense of togetherness.
